past.description:
Aztecsoft, started by S Parthasarathy and V R Govindarajan, was my first venture into startups. I was a founder member of the company. The vision of AztecSoft was to be a successful product company based out of India.

Joined as GM, R&D, I led the team to develop JPact, a Java based application server, conceived before the days of EJBs and J2EE. JPact was initially a multi-tier DSS product and eventually turned into a full-fledged application server with its own component-container model.

I subsequently architected Aztec ListServer Framework, a domain-specific solution on top of JPact App Server.

This was followed by various components and frameworks, such as ABIF (Aztec Business Integration Framework), which helped rapid development of applications by e-com startups.

Aztecsoft became closely associated with the e-com wave. Our team started working as an extension of the product development teams of our customers. Aztecsoft eventually perfected this model, creating a new category called OPD (Outsourced Product Development). I was engaged as a Solution Architect for multiple such customer products.

Aztecsoft went IPO in 2000, getting listed in BSE and NSE, and was acquired by Mindtree in 2008.
past.name: Aztecsoft
past.title: VP, Research

past.description:
Engineering & Scientific Subroutine Library (ESSL) Optimization [JAN 93 - AUG 93]
I worked as a team member at IBM T. J. Watson Research Lab, NY, USA, on optimization of ESSL for the IBM POWER2 RISC architecture. The objective was to hand-optimize the ESSL routines so that for the architecture they perform close to the theoretical peak.  This was achieved by significant algorithmic changes in the ESSL code, followed by appropriate compiler options for use of specific hardware features, while keeping the source code for the library in FORTRAN 77.

PVS system software [SEP 93 - SEP 94]
I worked as a team member at IBM T. J. Watson Research Lab, NY, USA, on system software development for the IBM POWER Visualization System (PVS). PVS was a shared-memory based multiprocessor, capable of running applications that require high data bandwidth coupled with supercomputer-class computational ability. My projects involved development of:
•  Videomedia V-Lan interface library, which provided a common language to communicate to the Digital tape Recorders
•  Driver interface for a high performance video I/O card, capable of doing several D1 movie I/O in real time.

Tape file system [DEC 94 - JUL 95]
I worked as the Project Leader to develop a product called Phoenix, for IBM Tucson, AZ, USA.  The objective was to develop a file system on a tape jukebox, having multiple sequential tape drives and magazines of tapes, and equipped with automated media changer. The scope also included providing an API in C/C++ and GUI for ease of use.

DataLinks [APR 96 – APR 97]
This project was done for IBM Almaden, CA, USA. Considering that most of world’s data reside in file systems, not database, a new data type was required in IBM DB2 database which could tightly link the two, providing transactional integrity. This new datatype was called DataLinks. I worked on enhancing DB2 for providing support for the same. Several database libraries and utilities such as LOAD were enhanced in the process.
past.name: IBM
past.title: Software Specialist

past.description:
C compiler test suite [DEC 89 - MAY 90]
I worked as an independent developer at the Santa Clara software development site of Intel Corp. on the design and development of ORION, an architecture specific test suite for the Portland Group i860 C compiler. The main objective was to test code generation using software pipelining algorithm tuned for the said architecture. ORION consisted of
•  Static programs with different types of loops
•  A powerful program generator to generate loops with common subexpressions on random pattern or based on user specifications.

ABI verification suite [NOV 90 - FEB 92]
I worked as the Project Leader for iBCS2/psABI386 (Intel386 Binary Compatibility Specification 2 and Processor Specific Application Binary Interface Specification for Intel386 Architecture) Verification Suites development. The assignment was entirely carried out in India. The aim of these test suites was to standardize and stabilize UNIX System V Releases 4.3 and 4.4, so as to provide binary compatibility to applications.

Automation was done wherever feasible. A large part of the test suite was generated from Standard C Header files and other system information. The corresponding documentation in nroff-format was also generated.

MAIDA-SQL [MAR 92 - SEP 92]
I worked as the Project Leader to develop MAIDA-SQL, a tool for visual development of RDBMS-based end user applications. This job was done for ILOG Corp., France, using their GUI toolkit running on a wide range of platforms.  Programming was done in LeLisp, a dialect of LISP with object-oriented flavors. The work was executed partly in France and partly in India.
past.name: Wipro
past.title: Software Specialist

past.description:
FORTRAN 77 Compiler under UNIX [APR 87 - JAN 88, AUG 88 - NOV 89, JUN 90 - OCT 90]

I worked as a member of the Compiler Group to do design and development of FORTRAN 77 compiler under UNIX platforms.  This work in various phases continued for three years.

Initial years of work, done as a team member, were on
•  Conversion of IR code generated by compiler front-end to AST, for code generation under Motorola 68020 processor
•  Revamping of the run-time libraries for both Intel i386 and Motorola processors, including use of math co-processors

Thereafter I proposed a new optimizing table-driven code generator based on Steve Tjiang’s work on a dynamic programming tool called TWIG (Ref: ACM TOPLAS Oct 1989). The proposal was accepted, and I started the development process with a small team. We developed TWIG in-house based on the specifications. Afterwards we developed the code generator using TWIG for the i386 architecture. The code generator was designed to convert ASTs to DAGs within Basic Blocks, perform several local optimizations including constant folding, algebraic transformations, common subexpression elimination, strength reduction and a few loop optimizations, and then convert DAGs back to trees for feeding to TWIG.  TWIG architectural specification was tailored to produce high quality locally optimized code. The performance of this compiler was comparable to the other FORTRAN 77 compilers in the international market.

After the release of the TWIG-based i386 compiler, we retargeted the compiler to Motorola Mc680x0.

COMMON LISP interpreter [FEB 88 - NOV 88]
I worked as the team leader for the design and implementation of a COMMON LISP (subset) interpreter, running under UNIX. The interpreter supported all the essential control structures and data types.  Nearly 60% of the standard COMMON LISP functions were implemented. A debugger and a LISP editor were among the major utilities supported as part of the LISP environment.
